# Parser fixtures

`traffic.log`, `url.log`, `system.log`, and configuration fixtures are constructed standard-format examples based on the official field references.

`pa1410-12.1-traffic.log` and `pa1410-12.1-dns.log` derive their field count/order and native family/subtype from actual PA-1410 PAN-OS 12.1.4-h8 Syslog captures. The native layouts contain 130 and 140 fields, respectively. **Every customer-identifying value was replaced or cleared**, including all original timestamps, addresses, usernames, rule names, serials, interfaces, URLs, threat identifiers, hostnames, UUIDs, and unknown trailing fields. Public protocol/application/action/subtype/category tokens remain to preserve interpretation. Counts, ports, session IDs, and other numerical values are fixed test data. Original captures are not in this repository.

Four additional 140-field layouts come from independently matched native/stored events: `pa1410-12.1-ml-virus-reset-both.log`, `pa1410-12.1-file-alert.log`, `pa1410-12.1-file-deny.log`, and `pa1410-12.1-wildfire-allow.log`. They cover a non-DNS Threat detection, permitted/denied File Blocking records classified as Data Filtering, and a historical benign WildFire submission. These are separate from `wildfire-virus` Threat detections; File Blocking coverage does not establish native `data` or `dlp` coverage.

The additional fixtures were built from blank arrays with the original field count. Only explicitly allowed public wire, subtype, application, protocol, action, category, severity, direction, file-type, and threat-category tokens were retained. Every other value was replaced with fixed test data or cleared, including all 32 unknown trailing fields. The digest, detection identifier, quoted rule/filename, addresses, timestamps, usernames, and identifiers are synthetic replacements. Original captures and private comparison records are not in this repository.

Tests assert addresses, ports, application, action, subtype/category, verdict/severity, file metadata, timestamps and offsets, byte/packet counters, and extension tolerance. Separate private validation compared actual stored values against matching firewall XML API log sequences. These fixtures establish reproducible parser coverage; they do not establish a fresh WildFire submission or complete transport, UI/export, or appliance acceptance. See `docs/validation/PALO_REAL.md`.
